prerequisites: Having previously taken the subjects Mathematics I and Mathematics II of the Degree

learning_outcomes.text: Model simple situations and apply appropriate techniques to solve the posed problems.
Use exact and approximate mathematical techniques.
Interpret solutions in mathematical terms within the context of the real problems posed.
Understand the principles of differential equations and statistical techniques in the field of Engineering.
Show students the correct way to choose appropriate techniques to address real problems, while instructing them in the use of suitable software for processing information to be studied in each case.
Show students the correct way to collect, order, analyze, and interpret information so that precise decisions can be made on issues they will encounter in their professional work.
Comprehension and interpretation of texts and data, development of skills for their concretization and clear and succinct exposition.
Aptitude for the distribution of resources and time and their implementation in real situations.
Ability to transmit concepts, ideas, processes, etc., related to Industrial Engineering orally and in writing, clearly and correctly.
Ability to use scientific-technical tools for solving calculation and design problems in Industrial Engineering and aptitude for finding sustainable engineering solutions.
Ability to work collaboratively and capacity for developing multidisciplinary projects.
Ability to relate to other people and an open attitude towards creating new relationships.
Aptitude for professional integration in diverse environments and with varied functions in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Ability to incorporate new knowledge in the area of Industrial Engineering, based on acquired training and necessary for the evolution of technique.
Development of autonomy and creativity capacities, fostering aptitudes for developing own initiatives and undertaking new projects.

Ability to solve mathematical problems that may arise in engineering. Aptitude to apply knowledge about: linear algebra; geometry; differential geometry; differential and integral calculus; differential and partial differential equations; numerical methods; numerical algorithms; statistics and optimization.

syllabus_topics: 2.2.- Study of random variables. Most notable variable distributions
2.3.- Statistical Inference: estimation and decision techniques
teaching_methods: Large Group Activity: Exposition, explanation and exemplification of contents. Lecture and problem solving by the professor.
Medium Group Activity: Problem and/or case study resolution. Lecture and problem solving by the professor.

Small Group Activity / practicals and seminars: Problem solving by students and computer practicals. Group work. Practicals in small groups on the knowledge shown in theoretical and problem classes. Computer practicals.
Tutorials: Individual / Group. Personalized follow-up of student learning.
Performing exams. Development of evaluation instruments.
Non-contact activities: Personal study. Report writing. Assignments. Problem solving. Exam preparation.
assessment_rules: Evaluation will be governed by the Evaluation Regulations of the University of Salamanca. The grading system currently in force (RD 1125/2003) article 5º will be used. It is recommended to carry out activities suggested by the professor during autonomous study hours and to attend classes and tutorials.
